title: Progressive Memory Slicing and Micro-fallback Lanes for OOM Resilience
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We continue to see tail OOMs on multi-tenant hosts during spikes of long-context streaming requests. Symptoms: sudden batch admission spikes, KV cache pressure, and slow host-spill causing request failures or 5xxs. Goal: introduce a layered OOM prevention and graceful recovery system combining (1) progressive memory slicing (dynamic context contraction), (2) KV cache reclamation tiers with async host snapshots, (3) micro-fallback model lanes (low-cost quantized variants) and (4) a fast soft-retry policy so downstream apps see minimal disruption. Success criteria: reduce OOM-induced 5xxs by >= 90% under the 99.9th-percentile traffic bursts in our stage stress rig, keep median latency increase <= 7% for requests hitting fallbacks, and avoid throughput regression >5% for normal traffic.
proposed_solution:
1) Admission controller enhancement: continuous batching changes to expose per-batch GPU headroom estimate and probabilistic admission that trims low-priority tokens when headroom < 15%.
2) KV cache tiers: implement hot/cold/evictable buckets. Evictable entries are async-snapshotted to host (NVMe) compressed checkpoints; reclamation is incremental and non-blocking.
3) Progressive context slicing: for long prompts we apply a ranked-trimming policy (remove low-salience trailing segments and auxiliary system prompts first) with a fidelity scoring function to stay within memory budget while preserving model correctness.
4) Micro-fallback lanes: lightweight quantized variants (redwood-compact-v1-4bit) are kept in deduplicated compressed loaders; requests are transparently downgraded when GPU headroom falls below 6% and KV reclamation cannot free space within 200ms.
5) Soft-retry & hedging: implement exponential backoff with jitter for short-lived OOM hits and single-step hedging: spin up fallback call in parallel if primary doesn't respond within (latency_slo*0.6) and primary failure inferred as OOM.
acceptance_criteria: Stage stress rig shows >= 90% reduction in OOM 5xxs at 99.9th percentile compared to baseline
Median latency increase for fallback-affected requests <= 7%
No throughput regression >5% on steady-state traffic
Canary rollout with runtime-1.24 preserves SLA for 95% of routes
Runbook and post-incident detection alerts published and reviewed by SRE
decisions: Use three KV cache tiers (hot/cold/evictable) with async snapshots to host rather than immediate full eviction - approved 2026-02-18
Reserve a conservative GPU headroom floor of 10% for background operations (kernels, memcopy) - aligns with kernel scheduler team guidance
Fallback model selection: redwood-compact-v1-4bit chosen as first-tier fallback due to 3x memory reduction and acceptable quality on our prompt-set - QA validated (see links)
Backoff windows: initial retry delay 50ms, multiplier 2.0, max retry 3 attempts for transient OOMs
risks_and_tradeoffs: Progressive trimming risks reducing model output fidelity on adversarial prompts; we mitigate by a fidelity score and guardrails to prefer KV reclamation first.
Async host snapshotting adds I/O pressure; we will schedule snapshot transfers under background QoS and throttle per-host to avoid NVMe saturation.
Maintaining fallback model weights increases storage and start-up complexity; we keep deduped compressed bundles and lazy-load on warmstart to reduce memory footprint.
Increased control plane complexity for routing/hedging requires careful observability to debug regressions during rollout.
